You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

 "content": "# Continual-ARC: fill framed interior using two external color keys

Observed solved instance task-de066aa6 (2026-10-22). A hollow 6x6 square frame (outline color 5) encloses a 4x4 empty area. Two colored single-cell keys sit outside below the frame, aligned near opposite sides: left key color A, right key color B. Fill the 4x4 interior as four 2x2 blocks: upper-left and lower-right get A; upper-right and lower-left get B (checkerboard quadrants). Preserve outline and external keys, and leave all other cells unchanged.

Evidence: demo had A=4 at row 1 col 1 and B=8 at row 1 col 8 (0-indexed); interior rows 3-6, cols 3-6 became `4 4 8 8` for first two rows and `8 8 4 4` for last two. Test used A=9 left and B=1 right at row 8; same spatial pattern. First test submission incorrectly assigned the reverse diagonal (A on upper-right/lower-left), while swapping the two colors across the two diagonal pairs was accepted. Thus left/right position of the keys alone does not determine upper-left color; upper-left/lower-right take the left key color, and the other diagonal takes right key color.
"
